_doc: District list of the seamless Kalesh map, as signed (architecture sign-off 2026-11-11; decisions.md 'One seamless open city, no gaps' and 'Architecture record (P0-022)'; MAP_REPAIR.md 'District frames and stitching'; TECH.md 'World layout'). Read by tools/bake/layout/ (P1-008). A block is one continuous piece of the map with one frame and one road graph. A district is a focus area inside a block (hand-drawn outline, hero roads, inspector review): an outline, not a cut and not a frame. Everything between focus districts inside a block is real city from the same sources. Placement method: offset = pivot.world + block.factor x geoToWorld(block frame origin, pivot). The centre block has factor 1.0, so every real place in it sits at its real position relative to India Gate; each far district is its own block at factor 0.5, on its real bearing from India Gate. A real point lands at offset + geoToWorld(lat, lon, block frame origin): a translation only, with no rotation, scale or mirror, north is -Z. The offsets in this file are a record to 0.1 m: the bake computes them from the method and rule R-STITCH fails if a recorded one differs. A far block keeps its real ground with one height offset solved over all its joins; the centre block has one ground model and one height solve. 'planned' lists focus districts that have a block but no focus outline or data yet; they move into 'districts' when their outline is drawn. The island layout of the Phase 0 stitch bench (layout C boxes, per-district frames and offsets, draft rectangles, the stand-in river) was removed from this file in P1-008; the measured results stay in decisions_archive.md 'Map stitch results (P0-029)'.

signed.quote: Yes, I sign off on the architecture.
signed.answers: Centre at true scale (factor 1.0); far south on its real bearing from India Gate at 0.5 of real distance (decisions.md 'Architecture answers, round 2')

method.rule: offset = pivot.world + block.factor * geoToWorld(frameOrigin, pivot), tools/geo/projection.ts; code tools/bake/layout/placement.ts

gates.note: Rule R-STITCH (tools/bake/layout/gate.ts), run in every bake before tiles are written and by tools/bake/layout/layout.test.ts. Centre pairs: every pair of the centre places in districts/places.json keeps its real bearing and distance (geodesic on the ellipsoid). Far blocks: each frame origin is on its real bearing from the pivot at farFactor times its real distance. A centre place paired with a far place may be off by up to about 20 degrees at factor 0.5 (computed, ARCH_OPTIONS.md 'The far south'); far places are exact as seen from India Gate. mapWidthMaxKm and reachMaxKm are FP1: a 32-bit float keeps 0.49 mm steps up to 8,192 m (2 to the 13th), the band measured fine at 7 km, and 0.98 mm beyond; a wider map needs a new measurement. Measured in P1-008 with every planned block placed: map box 13.03 by 13.37 km; the smallest circle round the map has a radius of 7.98 km (Cyber City, Laxmi Nagar and Kashmere Gate set it), so no world origin gets every position under 8 km by more than a few metres; the centre of the map box would leave Cyber City 9.0 km out. blockGapMinM: two placed block outlines stay this far apart, room for an edge band of up to 100 m on each block and a corridor between them.

method.worldOrigin: the centre of the layout C map box for now (India Gate sits at x 621.6, z 467.2). The first bake that includes a far block (P8) runs the recentre step (tools/bake/layout/recentre.ts): one vector, a whole number of 250 m tiles, is subtracted from every stored position (the pivot, tiles, pins, mission anchors, connector points, saves), so the world origin sits on the centre of the smallest circle round the final map and no position is more than about 8 km out (FP1). Not the centre of the map box: measured in P1-008, that leaves Cyber City 9.0 km out.

grid.note: The one world grid (tools/bake/layout/grid.ts): tile ids come from world metres, tile (0, 0) has its north-west corner on the world origin. A recentre moves the origin by a whole number of tiles.

stages._doc: Bake stages (P1-007, TECH.md 'World layout' Stages): `npm run bake -- <stage>`. A stage is one continuous outline inside a block. Every source is fetched once for the outline's box plus the margin (one continuous extract) into dataDir (gitignored) and pinned in data/SOURCES.json. ground: GEDTM30 smoothed over smoothM metres, filtered Copernicus GLO-30 as the fallback; FABDEM is never read.
